extraction.name: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, enabling a more rigorous evaluation of large language models (LLMs). It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). These tasks cover key long-text application areas including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, allowing for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs. LongBench-E is also constructed, featuring a more even length distribution, thus suited for gauging each model’s capability across various context lengths.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench is composed of 6 major task categories and 21 different tasks. 6 datasets are directly extracted from original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by the authors. Data extraction from public datasets is performed from their test sets to avoid test leakage, with the exception of VCSUM. Two extraction strategies are employed: random sampling to maintain a natural length distribution for LongBench, and uniform sampling based on data length (0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+) for LongBench-E.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original datasets from previous studies (e.g., NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, RepoBench-P), Wikipedia, Baidu Search, U.S. Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports, GitHub, C4 Dataset, Arxiv, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Chinese Government Website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Multi-Doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs are used as context. Distracting passages are added until a maximum length is reached, and passages are randomly ordered. For DuReader, several documents related to the question and arbitrarily selected distractors are associated with each question until 20 documents are reached. For MultiNews, 'Document i' is included before the i-th news article, and they are concatenated. For Few-shot Learning, a random number of samples from the training set are concatenated to form the context. For Synthetic tasks, 30 passages are randomly sampled, and one is summarized using GPT-3.5-Turbo. For PassageCount, several passages from English Wikipedia are randomly selected, repeated several times, and shuffled. For Code Completion (RepoBench-P), cross-file code snippets (including the gold snippet) are shuffled and combined into context C.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format. Passages in TriviaQA with less than 1,000 words are filtered to be examples. Data is extracted from the test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage, except for VCSUM. Random sampling is used for LongBench, and uniform sampling (based on word count for English/code datasets and character count for Chinese datasets) is used for LongBench-E, sampling comparable quantities from length ranges of 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA, three Ph.D. students annotated questions and answers for each article, aiming for definitive and relatively short answers suitable for automated evaluation. Annotators ensured answers could be inferred from documents and that evidence placement was random to avoid positional biases. For RepoBench-P, the optimal cross-file code snippet for prediction was manually annotated as the 'gold' snippet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators for MultiFieldQA showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For MultiFieldQA, three human annotators per item (question and answer).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP, positioned as expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used for summarization of selected passages in the PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh synthetic tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Memorization performance on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue is relatively high, likely because these datasets are derived from Wikipedia, a common source for training prevalent LLMs. This suggests models might rely on memorization rather than true context understanding for these specific tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: (1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics: Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect the quality of the response, especially for models generating longer responses, potentially underestimating their performance. (2) Coupling with instruction-following capabilities: The benchmark's performance is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, as real-world application tasks inevitably demand this, even though the primary objective is to assess long-context modeling proficiency.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: LongBench is a benchmark tailored for evaluating long context understanding of LLMs. It is used for testing and evaluation of LLMs, serving as an ideal testbed for future research in long context modeling. The assessment is conducted in a zero-shot setting, except for few-shot learning tasks where examples are provided as part of the long context.
